claim: Inspecting user services with plain 'systemctl status' fails; you must pass --user, and running 'systemctl --user' as root (including via sudo -i) fails with 'Failed to connect to user scope bus: No medium found' because root has no live user-manager bus — machinectl shell <user>@ is the correct way to inspect another user's units
stance_target: user-scoped services carry operational traps for fleet tooling/automation that system services avoid
evidence_type: anecdotal (worked forum example with verbatim errors)
quoted_support: running 'systemctl --user' as root (incl. via sudo -i) fails with 'Failed to connect to user scope bus: No medium found' because root has no live user-manager bus; machinectl shell <user>@ is the correct way to inspect another user's units

claim: Setting serviceConfig.User inside a systemd user unit fails — user services necessarily run as the owning user ('Failed to determine supplementary groups: Operation not permitted', status=216/GROUP)
stance_target: using serviceConfig.User inside a user unit to scope an agent's privileges (it is a system-unit-only field)
evidence_type: anecdotal (worked forum example with verbatim error)
quoted_support: setting serviceConfig.User inside a user unit fails — user services necessarily run as the owning user ('Failed to determine supplementary groups: Operation not permitted', status=216/GROUP)

claim: systemd.user.* installs the unit for ALL users under /run/current-system/sw/lib/systemd/user/; per-user installation requires home-manager (masking per user is manual)
stance_target: per-user installs of a NixOS user-service agent are not natively supported; home-manager is the per-user mechanism
quoted_support: systemd.user.* installs the unit for ALL users under /run/current-system/sw/lib/systemd/user/; per-user installation requires home-manager (masking per user is manual)

claim: home-manager errors on collision when a manually-created unit file exists in ~/.config/systemd/user; the fix is 'home-manager switch -b backup'
stance_target: migration from hand-written units to home-manager-managed units
quoted_support: home-manager collision errors when a manually-created unit file exists in ~/.config/systemd/user — fixed with 'home-manager switch -b backup'

claim: In user units use store paths (e.g. ${pkgs.coreutils}/bin/sleep) not /run/current-system paths, and %h instead of absolute home paths, for portability
stance_target: NixOS user-unit authoring conventions an agent's unit file must follow
quoted_support: use store paths (${pkgs.coreutils}/bin/sleep) not /run/current-system paths, and %h instead of automatic home paths for portability
